beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: A few weeks into rehearsals, Riley's back with a different question.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "My old band asked if I'd come back instead. I have to answer by tonight — but first I want to look at how I even got here."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You draw for the choice behind you.

options.text: Two real paths — the challenge was choosing, not lacking options.
It means one of those paths was objectively wrong.
This card can't say anything about a choice already made.

elaboration: The Lovers doesn't say one path was the mistake — it says both were real enough that choosing between them was the actual hard part, then and now.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "So tonight's answer is basically the same question all over again?"

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You draw for where you actually stand right now.

options.text: Not quite — you're standing somewhere new now, not repeating the old choice.
Yes, it's exactly the same decision again.
Where you stand now doesn't matter at all.

elaboration: The Fool in the present doesn't reopen the old fork — it just says you're mid-leap somewhere new, on ground the earlier choice helped create.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "On paper, going back makes more sense. But something about staying feels right."

options.text: Trust that feeling too — it says yes to the unknown instead of playing safe.
Only what makes sense on paper matters.

elaboration: The Fool doesn't ask for the sensible calculation — it asks whether you're still willing to say yes to not knowing exactly how this goes.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Okay. I think I already know what I'm telling them tonight. Thanks — that actually helped."
